name: Microsoft Entra ID sign-ins
description: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) sign-in records: who signed in, from where, with which client and app, and how it ended. One feed record for the SigninLogs table, the Splunk azure:aad:signin sourcetype and the dev sample table.
source: Microsoft Entra sign-in log schema; Azure Monitor Logs reference (SigninLogs); Microsoft Graph signIn resource; curated notes written for the Reach sample table

earliest.label: since
earliest.hint: On TimeGenerated (replay time for these samples, the connector's event time in production). SourceEventTime keeps the capture's own timestamp.

latest.label: until
latest.hint: Optional. Ingestion lags event time by minutes; a tight bound can miss the newest rows.

feed.label: Entra ID sign-ins
feed.description: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) sign-in log records, one per authentication attempt: who signed in, from where, with which client and app, and how it ended (ResultType).

created_date_time.label: Sign-in time
created_date_time.description: The capture's own timestamp. TimeGenerated is replay time in this dev workspace (the loader shifts each dataset so it is visible to ago(1d)); this column keeps when the event actually happened.

operation_name.label: Operation name
operation_name.description: The sign-in activity: Sign-in activity for interactive user sign-ins. Distinguishes user, non-interactive, service principal and managed identity sign-ins in the production tables.

category.label: Category
category.description: Log category the record belongs to: SignInLogs here. The record type of this table: NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs, ServicePrincipalSignInLogs and ManagedIdentitySignInLogs are the siblings in production.

tenant_id.label: Tenant id
tenant_id.description: The Entra tenant the sign-in was evaluated in. Differs from the workspace's TenantId column, which is the Log Analytics workspace id.

result_type.label: Result type
result_type.description: Sign-in outcome as an Entra error code: 0 is success; 50126 invalid credentials; 50053 locked or blocked; 50076/50074 MFA required; 53003 blocked by Conditional Access. The single most useful column for a spray: one code, many users.

values.50034: User account not found in the tenant
values.50053: Account locked, or sign-in from this IP blocked (too many failures)
values.50058: Silent sign-in interrupted; interactive sign-in required
values.50072: User must enrol for multi-factor authentication
values.50076: MFA required: new location or device
values.50125: Sign-in interrupted by a password reset
values.50133: Session invalid after a password change
values.51004: User account does not exist in the directory
values.530032: Blocked by Conditional Access on a security policy

result_signature.label: Result signature
result_signature.description: Short outcome label paired with ResultType (None on success, otherwise a short error name).

result_description.label: Result description
result_description.description: Human-readable outcome text. Free text; key on ResultType instead.

duration_ms.label: Duration (ms)
duration_ms.description: How long the sign-in took to evaluate, in milliseconds.

caller_ip.label: Caller IP address
caller_ip.description: Address the sign-in request came from. In a spray this is the one constant across every failed user. Proxies and VPN egress make one address many people; it is a lead, not a person.

correlation_id.label: Correlation id
correlation_id.description: Ties together every record of one sign-in flow (the interactive prompt, the MFA step, the token issue). Search it to see the whole flow.

identity.label: Identity
identity.description: Display name of the signing-in identity, as Entra renders it. Not unique; use UserId or UserPrincipalName.

severity_level.label: Severity level
severity_level.description: Diagnostic severity of the record (0 informational). Not the sign-in's risk.

country.label: Country
country.description: Country code derived from CallerIpAddress by Entra's geolocation. Derived, coarse, and wrong for VPN egress.

user_display_name.label: User display name
user_display_name.description: The user's display name at sign-in time. Changes with renames; UserId does not.

user_principal_name.label: User principal name
user_principal_name.description: The user's UPN (user@tenant). The key an analyst holds; UserId is the stable one underneath it.

user_id.label: User id
user_id.description: The user's Entra object id (GUID). Stable across UPN changes and renames.

app_id.label: Application id
app_id.description: Application (client) id the user signed in to. Well-known ids name Microsoft first-party clients (Office, Graph Explorer, Azure CLI…).

app_display_name.label: App display name
app_display_name.description: Display name of the application in AppId.

client_app_used.label: Client app used
client_app_used.description: How the client authenticated: Browser, Mobile Apps and Desktop clients, or a legacy protocol (Authenticated SMTP, IMAP, POP, Exchange ActiveSync, Other clients). Legacy protocols cannot do MFA; sprays target them.

user_agent.label: User agent
user_agent.description: The client's User-Agent string. Client-supplied and trivially spoofed; a spray tool often carries an odd or constant one.

conditional_access_status.label: Conditional access status
conditional_access_status.description: success, failure or notApplied: whether a Conditional Access policy applied to this sign-in and what it decided.

values.success: A Conditional Access policy applied and the sign-in satisfied it
values.failure: A Conditional Access policy applied and blocked the sign-in
values.notApplied: No Conditional Access policy applied to this sign-in

is_interactive.label: Is interactive
is_interactive.description: true when a person typed credentials; false for token refreshes and background sign-ins.

status.label: Status
status.description: Nested outcome object: errorCode, failureReason, additionalDetails. Status.errorCode duplicates ResultType as a number.

device_detail.label: Device detail
device_detail.description: Nested device object: deviceId, displayName, operatingSystem, browser, trustType. Empty for an unregistered device, which a spray always is.

location_details.label: Location details
location_details.description: Nested geolocation of CallerIpAddress: city, state, countryOrRegion, geoCoordinates. Derived from the address, not from the device.

authentication_details.label: Authentication details
authentication_details.description: Nested array of authentication steps (method, succeeded, resultDetail): the password step, then MFA if it got that far.

properties.label: Properties
properties.description: The connector's full properties bag, everything above and more (riskLevelDuringSignIn, riskState, tokenIssuerType…).

SigninLogs.note: The Entra ID diagnostic-settings table for interactive user sign-ins. Non-interactive, service-principal and managed-identity sign-ins land in sibling tables with the same shape.

azure:aad:signin.note: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services: the Graph signIn resource as JSON, nested objects flattened to dotted field names.

upn_renames.text: UserPrincipalName changes on rename and can be reassigned; UserId (the object id) is the stable key.

legacy_auth.text: Legacy protocols in ClientAppUsed (IMAP, POP, SMTP, ActiveSync) cannot complete MFA, which is why sprays target them; a success there is a real compromise, not an MFA-pending one.

ip_shared.text: One address is many people behind NAT, a proxy or a VPN egress. 'From this address' groups a network, not a person.

ua_client_supplied.text: User-Agent is set by the client and trivially spoofed. Use it to notice change, not to attribute.

edges.label: Every sign-in by this user
edges.basis_ref: Entra sign-in logs: one row per attempt keyed by the signing-in UPN
edges.note: Outcome, client and address per attempt, newest first.

edges.label: Sign-ins from this address, by user and outcome
edges.basis_ref: Entra sign-in logs: CallerIpAddress on every attempt
edges.note: A spray reads as many users, one code, from one address.

edges.label: Every record of this sign-in flow
edges.basis_ref: Entra: CorrelationId is shared by every record of one authentication flow

edges.label: Who signed in to this application
This address in other feeds
edges.basis_ref: Same address string; a NAT or proxy can put many people behind it
edges.note: Sign-ins and API calls from the same address are a lead, not a link.
